.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Hot weather continues into Monday, but relief is in sight 
later this week.

into evening. An isolated severe storm possible. Afterwards, we
remain dry the remainder of the week except for Wednesday night
into Thursday.

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1... 
A warm front will bring another round of warm, humid air into 
the area on Monday with highs in the upper 80s to mid 90s. Heat
indices will range 95 to 100 in areas of the heat advisory. 
Elsewhere, heat indices are anticipated to remain below 95. 

Following a cold front Monday, cooler air is expected to filter in 
with highs in the mid to upper 80s Tue-Thu, then down into the low 
80s by Friday. 


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
A warm front Monday will lead to a warm and unstable airmass 
over the area. Then a cold front is anticipated to pass through 
the area with shortwave energy aloft late afternoon into the 
evening. Ahead of it, PWATs will peak 1.9 to 2.1 inches. With 
the aid of lift from the front, a scattered to broken line of 
showers and thunderstorms is anticipated to track across the 
area west to east from 4 PM to 11 PM. The timing of the front is
still somewhat variable among the available among available 
model guidance. 

An isolated severe thunderstorm with brief downpours are 
possible. 12Z model soundings and available 12Z CAMs have a 
near- storm environment of 30 to 45 kt Bulk Shear, SBCAPE 
2500-3500 J/kg (some CAMs up to 4500 J/kg), DCAPE 900-1100 J/kg,
and peak 0-3km lapse rated of 8.2 to 9 C/km. 

For now, SPC has expanded a marginal (level 1/5) risk for 
severe thunderstorms over the western two-thirds of the CWA. 
This risk appears reasonable. The severe risk does appear to be
less if the front arrives too late in the evening, so it will 
really all hinge on the timing of the front. The primary risk 
with these severe storms will be straight-line damaging winds. 

The remainder of the week is anticipated to stay dry with only 
minor shots of any precipitation from passing shortwaves and 
fronts. The only good chance for another round of rainfall after
Monday appears to be Wednesday evening into Thursday.

&&

.AVIATION /03Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
A warm front lifts north of the terminals on Monday. A surface
trough likely moves across the area Monday afternoon and evening.

Mainly VFR. There is a chance for showers and thunderstorms late
Monday afternoon and early evening, mainly for terminals in the
vicinity of the NYC metro on N and W. Have continued with a
PROB30 for now as confidence remains low.

Light and variable flow expected through 12z. S flow develops 
thereafter, becoming S-SSW in the afternoon and evening 9-12 
kt.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments possible for PROB30 TSRA timing Monday 
afternoon/evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 00Z TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY...

Monday Night: Mainly VFR. Chance of showers and thunderstorms 
with brief MVFR in the early evening.

Tuesday-Wednesday: VFR. 

Wednesday Night-Thursday: Chance of showers and thunderstorms 
and MVFR. W gusts 15-20 kt possible on Thursday. 

Friday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

Winds and seas will remain below SCA levels through the middle of 
next week. 

Rip Currents: Lingering S-SE swells will lead to a moderate rip
current risk through Tuesday at ocean beaches.

.KEY MESSAGES...

this week. 

2) Showers and thunderstorms are possible late this afternoon 
and evening. The western half of the area is in a Marginal Risk
for both severe weather and excessive rainfall. 

3) Minor coastal flooding possible for some areas during the middle 
of this week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1... 
A warm front will bring another round of warm, humid air into 
the area today with highs in the 80s and 90s. Heat indices will
range from 95 to 100 in the heat advisory. Elsewhere, heat 
indices are anticipated to stay in the lower 90s. 

A cold frontal passage tngt will drop the humidity a little for
Tue. It will still be hot with highs in the 80s to around 90,
but heat indices should remain blw 95 with the drier air. Less
hot on Wed, as the entire area may stay blw 90 for the first
time since the 5th, then much cooler by the end of the week 
into the weekend with highs dropping blw climo by Fri.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
After a relatively cool start to the day, instability will
recharge this aftn in the wake of the warm front. Falling
heights would suggest developing shwrs and tstms this aftn and
eve across the area. The NAM and HRRR however have backed off a
bit on coverage. This looks like it is possibly due to
convective debris and subsidence from decaying activity over 
cntrl PA. Not totally convinced that this will have the impact 
modeled, and both the ECMWF and GFS have activity developing 
over the wrn portion of the area by 00Z. This times up with the 
convective wave over swrn MI, which is tracking ewd around 
25-30kt based on stlt, reaching the area. As a result, did not 
downgrade the NBM pops which bring in likely by 00Z wrn areas. 

The NAM convective parameters are not as impressive as previous
model runs, but this may be tied to the dissipating convection
over PA. With the area warm sectored and a lingering trof, the 
area will be in a favorable zone for severe into the eve. With 
pwats around 2, an isold flash flood risk remains, particularly 
NJ zones where hourly ffg is close to a half inch in spots and 
three hourly around an inch.

After today, there will be additional chances for shwrs and
tstms thru the week, as WNW flow aloft brings multiple vorts 
thru. Timing of these features is very low confidence, with the  
NBM struggling to keep up with the daily variations in the 
models. 

.KEY MESSAGE 3...
Astronomical tides will increase with an approaching new moon on 
Wednesday. Winds don't appear to be much of a factor with the 
evening/nighttime high tide cycles tonight through Wednesday night 
when minor flooding would be possible. A blend of 50th percentile 
NAEFS-based PETSS and NYHOPS seemed reasonable given recent trends. 
Flooding is therefore not anticipated tonight, but levels should 
come close to minor benchmarks for the south shore bays of Nassau 
County and Queens as well as Southern Fairfield County. With the 
astronomical tide a little higher Tuesday night, a Coastal Flood 
Statement could be needed for these areas. A better chance of an 
advisory would be during Wednesday night for these spots as flooding 
would be more widespread, and other spots including parts of NY 
Harbor and more of Western LI Sound could reach minor benchmarks as 
well.

&&

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
